preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `clean_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Complete the weapon_foundation increment by integrating the intact bound AK-74M and Saiga-12 first-person rigs and one authoritative, ordinarily controllable combat loop while preserving the accepted map, locomotion, camera, Alpha bindings, and clean boot.

diagnosis.root_cause: The candidate remains a locomotion-only FPS shell: Camera3D has no coupled hands-and-weapon instance, the InputMap has no combat actions, and no authoritative weapon/shot controller owns equipped weapon, per-weapon ammo, fire mode, reload, ballistics, or synchronized feedback. This is missing component and gameplay integration—not a transform-tuning defect.

stop_conditions: Stop and report a blocker if the already-bound registered package cannot be materialized with both intact gun/hand meshes, skeletons, AnimationLibrary resources, profiles, sockets, provenance, and receipt; do not substitute an unrelated package or modify authored children.

If telemetry and the rendered weapon disagree, stop transform tuning and identify the actual runtime-visible source beneath the camera before changing anything; calibration may affect only the whole-package adapter.

Do not continue if weapon work regresses clean boot, the single authored environment instance, collision/navigation, the accepted spawn-to-Alpha route, 76-degree camera behavior, locomotion states, or F6 reset/R reload separation.
Do not expand this iteration into enemy AI, final HUD/minimap, mission progression, decorative world changes, or authored-asset surgery.
Stop successfully when both required weapon-foundation checks pass with fresh candidate-bound evidence and clean_boot remains passing.

strategy.rationale: Materialize and directly instance the already-bound coupled viewmodel package, then connect it to a new authoritative weapon controller. This addresses the two absent systems together: the controller owns causal combat state while the intact package presents that state. Calibration is evidence-driven at one outer adapter only, and accepted world/locomotion systems remain isolated.

code: Developer verifies all candidate-owned scene, script, profile, animation, material, texture, audio, attribution, and receipt references resolve without modifying immutable imported children.
Confirm InputMap coverage for fire, ADS, reload, switch, fire mode, inspect, and gamepad equivalents; confirm R maps only to reload and F6 only to reset.

Inspect the controller path to prove per-weapon data isolation, SEMI press-edge scheduling, AUTO cadence/release cancellation, reload/switch cancellation, unique shot IDs, and exactly-once damage/ammo commits.
Run script/resource parsing and clean boot with no editor/runtime errors or missing resources.
runtime: From a fresh F6 run, Developer self-validates live groups and telemetry for viewmodels, weapon_controllers, equipped ID, action/animation state, ADS, fire mode, magazine/reserve, muzzle/optic transforms, shot ID, origin/direction, result, and damage commit.

Exercise AK hip/ADS, SEMI tap/hold, AUTO press/hold/release, tactical reload, empty reload, dry fire, and inspect; then switch to Saiga-12, repeat hip/ADS/fire/reload/dry fire, switch back, and verify each weapon retained independent ammo, mode, cadence, and visible source.
Use controlled geometry/target scenarios to capture blocked, miss, and hit results, verifying one event chain and one ammo decrement per accepted shot with no duplicate damage or presentation.

GameLoop Runtime and Tester rerun validate:weapon_foundation_viewmodel_spatial_integrity, validate:weapon_foundation_combat_causality, and validate:clean_boot; formal issue and phase closure remain theirs.
visual: Tester recaptures matched 1280x720 shipped-camera frames for both weapons in hip and settled ADS, identifying the runtime-visible source and confirming grounded realistic scale, two-hand contact, forward muzzle, aligned sight line, and clip-free framing.
Capture adjacent event windows for fire/recoil, tactical and empty reload contact, inspect, and switching—onset, peak/contact, and recovery—paired with distinct runtime state/timestamps.

Confirm the weapon silhouette visibly changes between AK-74M and Saiga-12, the foreground is no longer empty, and neither rig blocks the central sight line or lower-center interaction space suggested by the PRD reference.
Recheck representative spawn and Alpha-route views to ensure the intact authored environment, camera composition, locomotion, and objective bindings remain unchanged.

done_when: Fresh gameplay exposes one camera-child viewmodel host containing complete, runtime-visible AK-74M and Saiga-12 hands/weapon rigs, their Skeleton3D and animation resources, verified muzzle/optic/grip/magazine sockets, and truthful equipped-weapon telemetry.

Ordinary keyboard/mouse and gamepad-equivalent input demonstrates both weapons, bidirectional switching, hip/ADS, fire-mode switching, AK semi and automatic scheduling, Saiga firing with its own data, tactical and empty reload, dry fire, inspect, recoil recovery, and cancellation on switch, reload, reset, or unavailable combat state.

Every accepted shot has one stable shot ID and exactly one ammo deduction, origin/direction selection, blocked/miss/hit result, damage commit when applicable, muzzle flash, fire animation, recoil, one shot sound, impact response, and telemetry update; holding/releasing AUTO and press-edge SEMI obey their authoritative cadence.

At 1280x720, both intact rigs read as grounded realistic first-person weapons: hands maintain authored contacts, muzzle and sight point into the scene, ADS is aligned, required weapon parts remain readable, the near plane does not clip them, and fire/reload/switch transient poses do not expose broken arm or mesh edges. The center sight line and lower-center gameplay space remain clear, consistent.
tasks.instructions:
Preserve the accepted authored Standoff environment, outer datum, navigation/collision, Alpha Area3D bindings, prototype locomotion, camera, and deterministic F6 reset. Materialize the complete already-bound registered AK-74M/Saiga-12 coupled package into candidate-owned source with its provenance/receipt; keep each gun, hands, skeleton, AnimationLibrary, supplied clips, profiles, effects, and audio intact under a product-owned adapter. Instance the production viewmodel host directly beneath Camera3D and enumerate the actual visible descendants rather than trusting socket labels. Capture the raw imported-root baseline; change only one outer adapter/profile variable at a time if rendered bounds, forward vectors, optic line, or framing prove a defect—never rotate, scale, hide, detach, or edit authored children.

Add one authoritative weapon controller and state machine with separate AK-74M and Saiga-12 data for equipped ID, magazine/reserve, rate of fire, initial AUTO mode, alternate mode behavior, reload timings, ballistics, muzzle/camera origin, and action state. Add non-conflicting fire, ADS, reload, switch, fire-mode, and inspect inputs with gamepad equivalents; physical R remains reload-only and F6 remains reset-only. SEMI submits exactly one shot per press edge; AUTO submits immediately, repeats at the configured cadence while held, and stops immediately on release. Switching must change the visible intact rig and retain independent weapon data. Implement hip, ADS, raise/switch, fire/recoil, tactical reload, empty reload, dry fire, inspect, and ammo-depleted presentation using real supplied clips where available.

Each shot must generate one immutable ID, perform a camera/muzzle-consistent ray query, classify blocked/miss/controlled-target hit, commit damage at most once, then fan out synchronized muzzle, recoil, animation, audio, impact, and minimal reticle/telemetry observers. Add only the bounded controlled target or impact support needed to prove causality; do not add enemy AI or final HUD. Expose viewمَ?
